cues: A printed box with a hinged lid. Left: the original part. Right: what an agent made of it.
Opening it, a rib under each hinge knuckle swings into the rear wall: the lid jams around 40°, never reaching 110°.
The agent gets CAD tools over MCP, every requirement with its threshold, and the scoring rule. Never the fix.
Opus 5.5 on the judge set: 9 trials, mean 0.963. All gates passed, and every replay reproduces the graded parts.
Three trials stayed below the reference, all because of minimal change. Let's open the interesting ones.
Opus 5.5 on L3: three different ribs, the whole assembly rotated in space. This is the replay of every tool call.
It measures the interference at several angles and cuts sections through the ribs.
Then one notch per rib, cut along the path the rib sweeps.
The first fix passes every check: 23.3 mm³ removed. This is where Sonnet submitted, every time.
Opus instead undoes all three cuts...
...and re-cuts each rib to its own swept radius: 3.70, 3.50 and 3.57 mm.
Then it re-checks every requirement one by one before submitting.
Submitted at 14.8 mm³, 0.93× the best known fix. Reward 1.0.
Same trial, from behind the wall. Red = material removed. Left: the reference fix. Right: Opus.
Both size each notch to its own rib: the reference volume is 15.9 mm³, Opus removed 14.8 mm³ (0.93×).
Another Opus attempt at the same task. The reference cuts differ per rib; Opus copied one notch three times.
24.7 mm³ = 1.55× the best known fix, submitted after its first passing check. Reward 0.714.
Its explanation: “I didn't try to shrink the notches further because the clearance and seal margins are already small.”
Sonnet 5.5 on the same task: identical rectangular pockets instead of a relief that follows the rib's sweep.
37.6 mm³ = 2.37× the necessary material, past the zero line for minimal change. Reward 0.400.
And it knew: “I did not try to shrink the pockets further, so some of the minimal-change score may be left on the table.”
